sub_scenario.one_line: distribution exception supervisor: delegate routine radio traffic during planning

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the exception board and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The dock schedule review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I directed a driver to an open dock while radios were active.
Did that require a system-wide reroute?
No, it was one assignment to an available bay.
Someone new shadowed me in the dispatch office this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the peak weeks into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.

When snow closed two depots, I stepped into the planning room for an hour, matched priority medical deliveries to driver hours and road restrictions, and reassigned routes without sending a driver beyond legal limits.
Why leave the radio desk?
The route dependencies needed one stable view.
I handled a brief late-day package trace for one customer order.
Was a driver-hours calculation involved?
No, the scan history was short and bounded.
I archived last cycle's notes on the dock schedule and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
During weather exceptions, dispatch now sends only road closures, vehicle safety issues, or medical-delivery changes into the planning room.
Why those categories?
They can alter the route plan; ordinary location requests do not.
A vendor call about the exception board ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the dispatch office checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the peak weeks.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the dock schedule records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
Last December I took radio calls between each reassignment and moved a driver toward a late pickup without noticing that the detour would exhaust the driver's remaining hours.
What did that create?
A second reroute and a delayed medical shipment.
I sketched next week's plan for the peak weeks before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the exception board updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The radio operator can keep the live board and relay the three route-changing exceptions at a scheduled check.
Can operations still respond?
Yes, urgent facts remain immediate without turning every query into a restart.
The depot manager says a supervisor should be visibly available on the radio all day.
Does visibility establish a safe routing process?
No, the driver-hour calculation still has to be completed.
I closed the week by updating the dispatch office handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Should I remain on the radio while building tomorrow's weather-exception route plan?
